summary: Iteration 33 verified the token-fallback fix for cross-site cookie blocking (Safari/iOS/macOS/Huawei). Backend: 15/15 pytest tests passed - login/register/google return access_token+refresh_token in JSON body, /api/auth/me works with only Authorization: Bearer header (no cookies), /api/auth/refresh accepts X-Refresh-Token header without cookie, /api/files/*?token=<access> authenticates via query token. Frontend (Playwright + page.route to strip Set-Cookie on every /api/** response + periodic context.clear_cookies): all 4 roles (admin, siswa, tutor, proktor) login successfully, reach their dashboards, persist session across page reload (tokens remain in localStorage), navigate to multiple protected pages, and produce zero non-auth 401 errors. Logout clears localStorage auth_access_token/auth_refresh_token (verified for admin, student, proctor; tutor logout button was not detected by test selectors but endpoint works per backend tests).
critical_code_review_comments: security.py _extract_token correctly checks Bearer -> cookie -> ?token= query param (good order).
routes_auth.py /refresh returns new access_token in JSON body AND also sets a cookie - cookie set is harmless but redundant for the Safari path; current behaviour is backwards-compatible.
api.js response interceptor strips access_token/refresh_token from user objects before React state receives them - verified: /auth/me responses never leak these tokens to UI state.
api.js interceptor correctly avoids retry on /auth/(login|refresh|logout|register) 401s to prevent loops.

media.js fileUrl appends token only for internal /api/files/* URLs and only when a token exists; token is URL-encoded. Note: access tokens placed in query strings can appear in server access logs / Referer headers; acceptable trade-off but worth documenting.
AuthContext logout calls clearTokens() AND the backend /auth/logout; frontend state is cleared even if backend call fails (good).

rca of the issue: RCA validated and fix confirmed: Prior to this change, auth relied solely on httpOnly SameSite=None cookies. Safari/iOS/Huawei block third-party cookies by default when the frontend and backend are on different registrable domains, so after login the Set-Cookie was dropped and all subsequent requests had no credentials -> 401. Mitigation implemented: dual delivery of tokens - cookies for Chromium-with-cookies users (backward compatible) AND access/refresh tokens in JSON body stored in localStorage with Authorization: Bearer header for other browsers. Query-param ?token= handles / file links that cannot send custom headers. All layers verified working.
